definition: Christopher Kenneth Ingle Williams (born 1960) is a professor at the School of Informatics, University of Edinburgh, working in Artificial intelligence, and particularly the areas of Machine learning and Computer vision.
details: Christopher Kenneth Ingle Williams (born 1960) is a professor at the School of Informatics, University of Edinburgh, working in Artificial intelligence, and particularly the areas of Machine learning and Computer vision.

explainer.lead: Christopher K. I. Williams is a Professor of computer science.
explainer.knownFor: He is best known for his work on Gaussian processes and for the book Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning, co-authored with Carl Rasmussen.

timeline.what: Williams received a BA in Physics and Theoretical Physics from the University of Cambridge in 1982, followed by Part III Mathematics (1983).
He obtained his MSc and PhD both in computer science, in 1990 and 1994, respectively.
Doctor of Philosophy, University of Toronto
In 1994, Williams moved to Aston University as a Research Fellow.
He moved to the University of Edinburgh in July 1998 and became Reader in 2000.
